label: D1 higher after a2 or reaching S1, lower after reward (esp. a1-S2-rewarded); D2 higher in S1.
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * np.abs(belief_lo) ;; (phase == GO) * (belief_cover < 5) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r")
explanation: Raw candidate n of unit 10 is almost entirely timing (high at D1/GO, very negative at D2; timing R^2 0.98). Beyond timing, its D1 value adds up the previous trial: higher if the previous choice was a2, higher if S1 was reached, lower if it was rewarded, with an extra strong dip after a1->S2 rewarded (rare-rewarded a1). At D2 it is higher when the reached state is S1. The free fit adds a small GO dip after two unrewarded trials in a row and weak GO belief terms (|belief_lo|, low belief_cover); these leave unexplained some large GO dips during long unrewarded runs with a2 choices. Belief log-odds as such adds little beyond last-trial cues. Observed-only; no future or model-output terms.

issues: The D1 claims hold up. With one weight of +0.139, the summed D1 term (prev a2 + prev S1 - prev rewarded) matches the D1 residual table well: a2 S1 u +0.293, a1 S1 u +0.131, a2 S2 u +0.144, a1 S2 r -0.366. The extra a1-S2-r dip is real: dropping it lowers test R^2 from 0.511 to 0.484.

The D2 claim 'higher in S1' is too coarse. The D2 residual by this choice x state is a1S1 +0.136, a2S1 +0.024, a1S2 -0.081, a2S2 -0.101, so the effect is mostly a1 -> S1 (common S1). Swapping (phase==D2)*(state==1) for (phase==D2)*(state==1)*(action==1) raises test R^2 from 0.511 to 0.533.

There is a missed history effect at D1. (phase==D1)*(tv('state',-2)==1) gets weight -0.10: D1 is lower when the trial two back reached S1. Adding it to the free fit raises test R^2 from 0.519 to 0.554. In the short form (with the D2 a1->S1 term) it gives 0.562 test, which beats the reported free fit (0.557).

The large GO dips are systematic and still unexplained. Raw GO values fall from about +0.9 to as low as -0.15 (residual down to -1.1) during runs of unrewarded a2 -> S1-rare trials, and these are the top worst-fit windows in misses. No observed term captures them: unrewarded-streak terms, last_is('a2 S1 u'), belief_lo, belief_lo*(prev_action==2) and belief_cover<5 each add at most 0.009 test R^2.

Misses on the recorded short form still show systematic D2 over-prediction after unrewarded previous trials (a2 S1 u -0.093, a2 S2 u -0.083, a1 S1 u -0.067) and D1 under-prediction on the first trial ('?' +0.112). The short form explains 0.51 against an observed-only additive ceiling of 0.79, so a large share of the explainable variance is left out.
